Field manual-read route completion dropped from a 0.95 target to 0.88 across 9200 accounts in the same window (E-03), pushing more accounts into estimate-substitution billing and accounting for the ESTIMATED-read share of disputed bills (1240/3025, 41%, E-01), though the majority ACTUAL-read share (59%) is still unexplained.
v2_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). Response-speed (E-04: within SLA) and tariff-change (E-02, E-06: none logged) causes are ruled out. Billing validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-10), changed the high-consumption check to compare raw register values against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling; this check rejects AMI imports for flagged accounts (import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and all 1184 flagged accounts carry bill_read_type=ESTIMATED (E-11), confirming BV-17's import-rejection mechanism converts flagged high-consumption reads into estimate-substituted bills, driving at least part of the ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill bucket (1240/3025, 41%, E-01). Field route-completion shortfall (E-03: 0.88 vs 0.95 target, 9200 accounts) cannot explain this bucket at scale: only 320 accounts were actually marked estimated last cycle (E-09), far below the ~1104 implied by the shortfall. Because BV-17's mechanism structurally produces only ESTIMATED-type outcomes (E-11), it cannot explain the larger ACTUAL-read dispute majority (1785/3025, 59%, E-01), which remains without a confirmed cause after tariff, response-speed, field-staffing-magnitude and BV-17 mechanisms are each ruled out or structurally excluded.
